review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an opinion that students who have the highest academic results should be rewarded by their school, while others think that students who show improvements are worthier to be rewarded. Personally, I strongly believe that rewarding for all of these students is far better since it can recognize both their effort.

Admittedly, students that show the best academic results are considerably worth to be given rewards. Initially, since students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they completely deserve their praises and privileges, and this also may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, which can propel towards overall academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Since students are exposed to this kind of competition early, they are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, and it naturally follows that they are enabled to achieve success in later life.

However, students who performance their progress also should be rewarded. Firstly, only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, it can cause others to think that their effort is futile since they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. In this sense, students can be proned to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened, which can gradually lose their incentive to study. Besides that, emphasizing improvements can also encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, being irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. Therefore, the constant desire to outdo themselves can even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that all of the efforts from students should be rewarded, regardless of showing the best academic results or just improvements.
review.overall: Em đã trả lời đủ hai quan điểm và giữ lập trường rằng trường nên ghi nhận cả thành tích cao lẫn sự tiến bộ. Thân bài 1 có hai hướng triển khai đúng: sự ghi nhận cho nỗ lực học tập và sự chuẩn bị cho cạnh tranh; thân bài 2 cũng nêu được nguy cơ nản chí khi chỉ một số ít được thưởng và lợi ích của việc ghi nhận tiến bộ. paragraphs: Opinions are divided over whether schools should reward academic excellence or give greater recognition to students who make progress. I believe that both groups should receive rewards because this recognizes high achievement as well as efforts to improve.

Admittedly, students who achieve the best academic results deserve their praises and privileges. Since they have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve such rewards, which may encourage both those students and their classmates to study harder and may lead to overall academic gains. Furthermore, competition exists in almost every aspect of life, where the best individuals are often rewarded. When students are exposed to this reality early, they can learn to thrive in the face of fierce competition and may be better prepared for success in later life.

However, students who show progress should also be rewarded. If only a few high-achieving students receive rewards, other students may feel that further efforts are futile because they cannot surpass these outstanding individuals. As a result, they may feel disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. By contrast, recognizing improvement can encourage all students to be diligent and to keep improving themselves, irrespective of their current performance. This desire to outdo themselves can create more lasting motivation than a determination to defeat others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that schools should reward both students who excel academically and those who make meaningful progress.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that public museums and art galleries will be replaced as soon by online websites since people can see historical objects and museum and gallery works of art by using computer. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, nowadays, technology can brings some new advantageous history and culture experience to people. One chief of those is that with high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms, people are enabled to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail, without leaving home. This can clearly seen in the case of Louvre museum, which allows visitors to approach and observe artefacts with realistic experience and details by its online websites. Furthermore, since that, those who cannot afford and have mobility issues can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums' and art galleries' benefits are irrefutable. Initially, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefacts or artwork in person, since it can evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For instance, when people visit museums that related to war, they can directly observe soldier uniform and listen to the stories from old soldiers, which can make them understand their sufferings. Moreover, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs, which symbolizes the identity of a region, it naturally follows that they can be magnets for tourism and a facilitator of bonding within the community.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that although people can see historical objects and works of art by using computer, public museums and art galleries cannot be replaced since it still brings some advantages that can find on online websites.

review.overall: Em viết đủ bốn phần và giữ đúng lập trường phản đối; câu chủ đề Body 1 thừa nhận lợi ích của công nghệ, Body 2 trở lại giá trị bảo tàng. Em cũng tự phát triển ví dụ về quân phục và lời kể của cựu binh. Tuy nhiên, những khung đã học vẫn sai nhiều: “technology can brings” sai modal + động từ, “This can clearly seen” thiếu be, còn “since it can evoke emotions” để nguồn cảm xúc mơ hồ và dễ đảo chiều ý. Câu kết “advantages that can find on online websites” lại đi ngược lập trường. Bài còn ẩu ở khâu tự soát: em cần nghiêm túc, cầu thị đọc từng chú thích, sửa đến đúng cấu trúc và kiểm lại nghĩa câu kết trước khi nộp.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that public museums and art galleries will become unnecessary since people can see historical objects and works of art on a computer. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, nowadays, technology can bring some beneficial experiences of history and culture to people. One chief benefit is that, with high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms, people are enabled to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail, without leaving home. This can clearly be seen in the case of Louvre museum, whose online website allows visitors to observe artefacts in realistic detail. Furthermore, those who cannot afford museum visits or have mobility issues can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums' and art galleries' benefits are irrefutable. Initially, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing artefacts or artwork in person, which can evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For instance, when people visit museums related to war, they can directly observe soldier uniforms and listen to stories told by veterans, helping visitors understand the soldiers' suffering. Moreover, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs which symbolize the identity of a region. This role makes them magnets for tourism and a facilitator of bonding within the community.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that although people can see historical objects and works of art on a computer, public museums and art galleries cannot be replaced, since they offer advantages that online websites cannot provide.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that governments should ban dangerous sports; some others argue that every individual should have rights to take part in any sports or activity they want. Personally, I am of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited since even a minor error can also lead to death of a participant, say, in skydiving, if they do not prepare carefully before participating or do not pay their attention to listen instruction, they may lose control their gravity and bodies. However, I believe that banning dangerous sports is not feasible and possible. Remote locations where some dangerous sports often take place, say, mountain cliffs have minimal surveillance and control, it naturally follows that governments or authorities can not know what happens here and control that. Besides that, it is also unrealistic to force a police officer follow every individual, in order to make sure they obey the rules. As a result, a prohibition will exist only on paper and even lead to a worse situation, dangerous sports practice underground, which is harder to ensure basic safety standards.

To add further credence to my assertion, I note that people should be permitted to do any sport, as long as they understand the risks and receive sufficient training. For instance, people who want to try deep-ocean diving and bungee jumping should enroll a course by reputable club, to which has appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Especially for new players, they should be accompanied by an expert and taught what to do when accidents occur, in order to recognise dangers and respond appropriately. Although proper training and necessary precautions can enable participants to be safer, no activity is entirely risk-free.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that instead of banning, which is neither practical nor effective, freedom to choose, provided under strict conditions of training and awareness would be more realistic approach.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that governments should ban dangerous sports; some others argue that every individual should have the right to take part in any sport or activity they want. Personally, I am of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited since even a minor error can lead to the death of a participant. In skydiving, someone who does not prepare carefully or pay attention to instructions may lose control during the jump. However, I believe that banning dangerous sports is neither feasible nor practical. Some dangerous sports take place in remote locations, say, mountain cliffs, where surveillance and control are minimal. Therefore, authorities cannot easily monitor what happens there. Besides that, it is unrealistic to expect a police officer to follow every individual in order to make sure they obey the rules. As a result, a prohibition may exist only on paper and may even lead to dangerous sports being practised underground, which makes it harder to ensure basic safety standards.

To add further credence to my assertion, I note that people should be permitted to do any sport, as long as they understand the risks and receive sufficient training. For instance, people who want to try deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping should enrol in a course at a reputable club that has appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Especially for new players, they should be accompanied by an expert and taught what to do when accidents occur in order to recognise dangers and respond appropriately. Although proper training and necessary precautions can make participation safer, no activity is entirely risk-free.
In conclusion, I strongly believe that a ban is neither practical nor effective. Freedom to choose under strict conditions of training and awareness would be a more realistic approach.

paragraphs: Some people argue that parents should allow children to learn through trial-and-error, while others believe that adults should help them avoid mistakes. Personally, I strongly believe that freedom to make mistakes should be encouraged, provided that errors do not involve serious danger.

Admittedly, opponents of a trial-and-error approach often emphasise that adults should prevent children from making mistakes. Since most mistakes, say, knives, fire or electricity are avoidable, so it is unnecessary for children to get hurt to learn to be more carefully. Moreover, shielding children from harm and forestalling mistakes can also make parents fulfil the duty of making sure their children's safety. And if pre-emptively help children avoid making mistakes, parents can enjoy peace of mind since they do their best to protect and raise their child.

However, those on the other side have their own valid reasoning to say that children should have the rights to make mistakes. Initially, parents cannot be around their children all the time, this means that they cannot protect their children completely when they experience new things and naturally making mistakes is inevitable. Furthermore, trying new things also help them get more invaluable lessons, which can stand them in good stead in later stages of life. Finally, if children are shielded from everything, they can be overdependent on others when they grow up, which is undesirable trait that can have negative impacts on their future lives.

Overall, it seems to me that allowing children to learn from mistakes means that parents prepare for their future, provided that they intervene and give guidance on important matters to prevent errors that may derail their future.

paragraphs: The given bar chart illustrates how much carbon emissions was generated by three different fossil fuels, namely oil, coal and gas over 20-years period, commencing from 1990 in the UK.
Overall, there was a gradually increase in the amount of carbon emissions from gas, while the opposite trend was observed in the case of oil and coal.

To elaborate, starting at 220 million tons in 1990, the amount of carbon emissions from gas rise gradually to 320 million in 2010, marking the highest point of the entire chart. Additionally, the most significant growth was also seen in the figure for gas, with 100 million tons through the period.

Regarding to the others categories, the most noticeable decline was witnessed in the amount of carbon emissions from coal, decreasing from 310 million tons to 190 million tons over the years. paragraphs.text: The bar chart shows the amount of carbon emitted by oil, coal and gas in the UK from 1990 to 2010. Figures are measured in millions of tons at five-year intervals.

Overall, emissions from gas rose throughout the period and became the highest of the three by 2000. By contrast, coal emissions fell steadily and ended at the lowest level, while oil emissions also declined overall despite a temporary recovery in the middle of the period.

Gas produced about 220 million tons of carbon emissions in 1990, the lowest figure among the fuels that year. The amount then increased at each recorded point, reaching approximately 300 million tons in 2000 and 320 million tons in 2010. Its total increase of about 100 million tons was the largest on the chart.

Coal followed the opposite pattern. Its emissions dropped from around 310 million tons in 1990 to 250 million in 2000, before falling further to roughly 190 million in 2010. Oil also ended lower than it began, but its decline was smaller: after falling from about 270 to 240 million tons between 1990 and 1995, it recovered to around 260 million in 2000 and then decreased to about 210 million in 2010. Thus, oil's overall fall was approximately 60 million tons, compared with about 120 million for coal.

task.text:
WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that history is one the most important school subjects, while others argue that science-related and technology-related subject are more crucial than history in today's world. Personally, I strongly believe that both this subjects have particular benefits.

On the one hand, history's benefits outweigh science and technology subjects on some sides. Initially, since history is compulsory subject in school, students can understand and have in-depth knowledge about culture and if they can find passion from this subjects, they can find their jobs in the future, say architecture or historic researchers, which plays an important roles in thriving country's history and also economic.

On the other hand, subjects like science and technology are more beneficial than history on the others side. Firstly, since students are exposed to subjects, say science or technology as school subjects, they can enhance critical thinking and problem-solving skills by dealing with this subjects' exercises, which plays an important roles in helping them solve future career problems if they choose major and jobs that relevant to technology and science. Furthermore, since important job sectors
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that all of the subjects have particular benefits that cannot overlap.
review.overall: Em đã bàn đến cả hai quan điểm và thể hiện ý riêng rằng lịch sử cũng như khoa học–công nghệ có giá trị riêng; đây là một lập trường hợp lệ. Ý về hiểu văn hóa và ý về rèn tư duy giải quyết vấn đề đều liên quan đề, nhưng em cần giải thích cụ thể hơn cách mỗi môn tạo ra lợi ích đó. Đoạn khoa học dừng giữa câu 'Furthermore, since important job sectors', làm luận điểm sau chưa thành hình. Khi sửa, em hãy hoàn tất ý trước khi kết luận và rà lại hòa hợp số ít/số nhiều trong cả hai đoạn thân bài.

criteria.label: Task Response
criteria.comment: Em đề cập cả góc nhìn coi trọng lịch sử và góc nhìn ưu tiên khoa học–công nghệ, đồng thời giữ quan điểm hai nhóm môn có lợi ích riêng. Những lý do về văn hóa, nghề liên quan lịch sử và kỹ năng giải quyết vấn đề có liên quan nhưng còn khái quát; ý mở thêm về 'job sectors' bị bỏ dở.

criteria.label: Coherence and Cohesion
criteria.comment: Bố cục mở bài–hai quan điểm–kết luận rõ và người đọc theo được hướng lập luận. On the one hand/On the other hand nối đúng hai mặt, song các câu dài dồn nhiều ý, lặp 'subjects' và câu Furthermore dừng ngang làm mạch đoạn ba yếu đi.

criteria.label: Lexical Resource
criteria.comment: Em dùng được các cụm theo chủ đề như in-depth knowledge, critical thinking, problem-solving skills. Tuy nhiên nhiều kết hợp thiếu tự nhiên hoặc thiếu chính xác, như find passion from, on some sides, historic researchers và benefits that cannot overlap.

criteria.label: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
criteria.comment: Em thử cấu trúc since, if, which và mệnh đề dài, nên ý chính phần lớn vẫn hiểu được. Lỗi dạng từ và hòa hợp lặp lại ở 'technology-related subject are', 'both this subjects', 'which plays an important roles', 'jobs that relevant'; một mệnh đề chưa được hoàn tất.

annotations.quote: which plays an important roles in helping them solve future career problems if they choose major and jobs that relevant to technology and science
annotations.title: Hòa hợp động từ và thiếu are trong mệnh đề quan hệ

annotations.quote: Furthermore, since important job sectors

annotations.explanation: Since mở đầu nguyên nhân nhưng em dừng trước khi nêu điều gì về các ngành nghề và kết quả của nguyên nhân ấy. Bản gốc thật sự dừng ở đây rồi sang kết luận; cần hoàn thành một ý có bằng chứng liên quan hoặc bỏ câu này.

annotations.quote: benefits that cannot overlap
annotations.title: Kết luận nên gọi rõ lợi ích khác nhau
annotations.explanation: Không phải lợi ích của các môn hoàn toàn không thể trùng nhau; em muốn nhấn mạnh mỗi nhóm môn có đóng góp riêng. 'Distinct benefits' nói đúng ý này mà không ép em chọn một bên.
annotations.replacement: distinct benefits that make both worth studying

paragraphs.text: Some people regard history as one of the most important subjects taught at school, whereas others believe science and technology matter more in the modern world. In my view, both areas of study have distinct benefits, and students need opportunities to learn from each of them.

On the one hand, history gives students a deeper understanding of the cultures and events that shaped their communities. Learning why people made particular decisions in the past can help young people understand traditions and make sense of current social debates. It may also lead some students towards careers linked to heritage. For example, a researcher might use historical records to explain the importance of an old building, while an architect working on its restoration would need to understand its original design. In these ways, studying history can support both cultural preservation and worthwhile employment.

On the other hand, science and technology can develop skills that students use to solve practical problems. When they carry out experiments or work through technical exercises, they learn to examine evidence, test possible answers and improve a solution that has failed. Such habits are useful for students who later choose scientific or technology-related careers. For instance, a technician may need to identify why a device does not work and then test a safe repair. Many other jobs also require some scientific knowledge, so these subjects can broaden students' choices after school.

In conclusion, I do not think schools should treat history and science as interchangeable. History strengthens cultural understanding, while science and technology build practical reasoning. Their different contributions make both valuable parts of education.
